title: Chain-Leader-Orchestrated Twin Transformation of Manufacturing Industry Chains: A Conceptual Framework with Illustrative Evidence from Xi'an, China
content: The twin transformation—the coordinated pursuit of smart (digital) and green (sustainable) manufacturing—has become a central agenda in manufacturing research and policy. However, existing studies operate almost exclusively at the firm level: how smart and green transformations are coordinated at the industry-chain level lacks a theoretical account, and the convergence (“ronghehua”) dimension prominent in Chinese industrial policy discourse has not been conceptualized. This article develops a conceptual framework of chain-leader-orchestrated twin transformation. It argues that chain-leader firms act as organizational intermediaries that supply chain-level public goods through four mechanisms—capability spillover, standard transmission, scenario orchestration, and factor orchestration—and that convergence, the integrative capacity spanning actors, chain stages, and chains, constitutes the organizational condition and amplifier of smart–green synergy. Three theoretical propositions are derived. Four publicly documented cases from Xi'an's manufacturing sector provide illustrative evidence. The framework extends twin transformation research from the firm to the industry-chain level and draws policy implications for inland central cities that organize industrial transformation around chain leaders and new factor endowments. Empirical testing of the propositions constitutes the agenda for future research.
